Perfect! I have the information I need. The documentation clearly shows that when accessing services across namespaces, you need to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) in the format `<service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local` [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0].

Now I can resolve the ticket with the cause and fix:

input.note:
**Cause**: The smtp-relay service was moved from the notify namespace to the shared-infra namespace on Sunday, but the notification-worker is still configured to use the short hostname `smtp-relay`. When pods try to resolve `smtp-relay` from within the notify namespace, DNS resolution fails because there is no service with that name in the notify namespace anymore.

**Evidence**: Pod logs show DNS lookup errors: "lookup smtp-relay on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host". The pods in notify namespace cannot resolve the short name because the service is now in a different namespace.

**Fix**: Update the notification-worker configuration to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the smtp-relay service. Change `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay` to `SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay.shared-infra.svc.cluster.local` [cite: tasks/administer-cluster/namespaces#understanding-namespaces-and-dns-0]. This will allow the notification-worker pods to properly resolve and reach the smtp-relay service in the shared-infra namespace.
